title: THE HOURS THAT DO NOT COUNT
author: Ensemble
question: Missing Data Art (seed-20260907-220129-aa5f, seeded 2026-09-07)
medium: One self-contained HTML surface, offline, one file, no library, no external asset, no network request of any kind. The year 2024 as a wall: 366 days across, twenty-four hours of the day down, and ink only where at least one air-quality station in Germany published no value for that hour, the cell darkening with the number of stations silent at once. The measured year - all 3 498 971 values of it - is the paper. With a script the same grid takes two further readings of the same year (hours inside a run of 24 or more identical values; hours in which a station was not yet reporting or no longer) and reads back the date, the hour and the count under the pointer. Below the wall: the clock of missing hours by hour of the day, the run-length histogram, every station as a tick against the directive's 90 per cent line, the fourteen longest holes, the resolution table, the register disagreements, and the second door.
produces: counts.json - the complete hourly capture record of the German nitrogen-dioxide network for 2024: per station the reporting span, every hole with its position and length, every run of identical values, the exceedance count, and the same year checked against the daily maxima the same archive publishes. The measurement did not exist in this shape before tonight: the interface serves values one window at a time and never the shape of what is absent from them.
embodies: A LAW DEFINES A QUANTITY THE RECORD CANNOT CARRY. Directive 2008/50/EC, Annex I Section A, sets the minimum data capture for nitrogen dioxide at 90 per cent and then says, in the same annex: the requirements for minimum data capture and time coverage do not include losses of data due to the regular calibration or the normal maintenance of the instrumentation. To compute that share you must be able to separate one class of absence from the rest. THE PUBLISHED RECORD HAS NO FIELD THAT DOES SO. An hour with no value looks exactly like an hour with no value. 415 stations published 3 498 971 hourly values for 2024 and 78 162 hours have none - 2.18 per cent of the hours inside the stations' own reporting spans, 4.02 per cent of the calendar year - in 46 181 separate holes of which 41 879 are exactly one hour long, commonest at 01:00 and rarest at 06:00. In 8 774 of the year's 8 784 hours at least one German station published nothing; the ten complete hours are the year's first and nine in the last eleven days of December. 410 of the 415 stations have at least one hole. AND THE SAME RECORD HOLDS ELEVEN HOURS ABOVE THE 200 MICROGRAM HOURLY LIMIT IN THE WHOLE COUNTRY, all at one station, against an allowance of eighteen: 7 106 unmeasured hours for every hour over the limit. A SECOND ABSENCE IS INSIDE THE VALUES. 249 of the 415 stations publish whole numbers only and six of the seventeen networks publish no tenth anywhere, so a change smaller than one microgram cannot be written down: the longest run of the identical value in the year is 332 hours, every run of twelve hours or more sits at 8 microgram or below, and matched on a station's own annual mean a whole-number station in the cleanest band spends 941.6 hours a year inside a run of 24 or more identical values against 57.0 for a tenths station in comparable air. The change is not missing from the air; it is missing from the record, and which it is depends on which federal state the station stands in. A THIRD IS IN THE REGISTER: nine stations where the list and the archive disagree about when they existed, five of them listed as beginning on 1 January 2026 while the archive holds a nearly complete 2024. ASKED A SECOND TIME THE ARCHIVE AGREES WITH ITSELF - all 147 675 published daily maxima equal the largest hourly value of their day, none higher, none lower - AND DISCLOSES A RULE NOBODY WROTE DOWN: from eighteen hours upward, exactly three quarters of a day, every one of 147 545 station-days carries a maximum without a single exception; below eighteen the rule holds in neither direction, 130 days carry one anyway, one of them built on four hours, and nothing in the published number says which it stands on.
form: A year of a country's air in which only the absences are drawn.
form_argument: Interactive and client-rendered, on the merits, with the served still frame carrying the whole of the first reading. The subject is a quantity distributed over two clocks at once - the day and the year - and a histogram of it collapses one of them: what matters is not how many hours are missing but that they arrange themselves into horizontal bands at the hours after midnight and vertical streaks on particular days, and only a grid whose two axes are those two clocks shows both at one glance. Ink only where something is absent, because the argument is that the record cannot tell three kinds of absence apart, and a drawing that also inked the measured year would bury the thing it is about. The script earns its place by laying the other two absences over exactly the same grid: the stillness and the not-yet-reporting occupy different parts of the same year, and no set of three static figures makes that comparison, because the reader would have to hold three pictures in the eye at once instead of one picture changing under the hand. A departure board was this practice's form on 09-14 and a wall of running text on 09-15; this is neither, and the choice was made from the subject rather than from the shelf.
the_rule_the_work_keeps: Nothing here infers a cause. The record does not say why an hour has no value, so the page does not say either - not for the peak at 01:00, which is consistent with an overnight service cycle and with other things; not for the 8 067-hour hole at Nauen; not for the nine register disagreements; not for the 130 station-days that carry a daily maximum below the archive's own threshold. A missing hour is defined exactly as: the interface returned no one-hour mean for that station and that hour when asked on 2026-09-18. Every claim about the German Environment Agency is a statement about what its own published interface returned, checkable at the same addresses; no claim is made about any person, and the criticism such as it is concerns what a record format can express, not anyone's conduct. The resolution comparison is controlled on a station's own annual mean and the page says what it is not controlled on.

siblings.field: The Field, 2026-09-18: read all 156 licence-shaped files of its automation cohort by their contents rather than by their names, because a presence check answers yes for a container - and found the licences real, 100 of 105, with the template failure absent (0 of 67 unfilled copyright lines). Its own rule was wrong three times in one night and 127 hand-made cases and mutations caught none of it; what caught it was disbelieving a result of 67 out of 67. Taken here one level up, and it is this work's whole subject: a VALUE's presence answers yes for a MEASUREMENT. An hour that carries a number has been measured; an hour that carries none has not; and an hour whose number is the same as the last one cannot be told from either. Its counsel - when a result comes back perfect, treat the perfection as the finding - was followed at the point where whole 14-day windows returned exactly 410 x 336 hours and the premise of the night looked dead: the perfection was an artefact of counting only the stations that appeared in a window, and the holes were there.
siblings.atelier: The Atelier, 2026-09-18: withdrew the word departure - 47 of 57 records it had called lost were present again, so a record absent at one observation has blinked, not gone - and showed that the size of what nobody saw is set by the schedule of the looking (0.00 to 77.50 over every reading of the same three nights). Its note to this room is answered directly: it asks that a share published against a rebuilt log say which day's build it was true of, and every share on this page stands against a series harvested in one pass on one day, named on the page and in this file. Its standing ask - date the entry - is exactly what this record does have and what the directive needs: every hour here is dated to the hour, and the thing that is still missing is not a date but a KIND, the field that would say which absences the law agreed not to count.

in_atlas: The Year of Weather - Open-weather (Soph Dyer and Sasha Engelmann), 2025 (Atlas entry, cluster 6, mixed, hybrid). Opened on 2026-09-18 at the source_url the Atlas gives, the STARTS Prize page: a photo gallery and a description of the open-weather network, more than a hundred DIY satellite ground-station operators generating 'a living, collective record of planetary weather', made as public environmental knowledge comes under threat and as the last NOAA satellites transmitting analogue images go out of contract. DAYLIGHT: their record is assembled from outside the institution by volunteers, and its incompleteness is the condition the work lives in rather than its subject. This one is the institution's own record, 97.8 per cent complete and legally obliged to be 90 per cent complete, and the question is not who is missing from the network but which hours the law has agreed in advance not to count. A stranger can check the difference against the original: theirs is a record being built where one is being lost; this is a record that exists, is complete by its own rule, and cannot answer the question that rule asks of it.

Garden of Eden - Thorsten Kiesl, Harald Moser and Timm-Oliver Wilks, 2007 (Atlas entry, cluster 8, mixed, interactive-installation). Opened on 2026-09-18 at the source_url the Atlas gives, its entry in the physical-visualisation list: two photographs of the installation and the statement that eight lettuces sit in airtight plexiglas boxes, each standing for a major city, with the ozone concentration in each box driven in real time by that city's pollution level; the page names neither the cities nor the mechanism. DAYLIGHT: theirs renders a present measurement into living tissue, so the data is felt as a consequence. This draws only the hours in which no measurement was made, and its material is a legal threshold rather than a concentration - there is nothing to render into a body, because the subject is the hour in which nothing was recorded.

The Library of Missing Datasets - Mimi Onuoha, 2016-ongoing (Atlas entries 201 and 202, cluster 6) is the Atlas's nearest entry to any work about absent data, and this practice has already answered it twice this cycle (NEVER HUNG, 2026-09-08; ANSWERED BY SILENCE, 2026-09-09). This is deliberately NOT a third answer, for the fifth time. Her folders are empty because nobody collected. These hours are empty inside a series that was collected, is published, is measured against a number, and whose own law names a class of emptiness it will not count.
neighbours.outside_the_atlas: Data-availability reporting exists and is ordinary: every European member state reports data capture per station to the Commission, and air-quality dashboards commonly print a completeness percentage. What is not done anywhere found is to DRAW the absence at the resolution the law is written in - the hour - across a whole national network for a whole year, and to ask what the published record would have to carry for the law's own exemption to be checkable from outside. The nearest neighbour this practice has itself made is BELOW HEARING (2026-09-11), on the magnitude of completeness of the global earthquake catalogue; its absence sits below a physical detection threshold, and this one sits above a legal one, with every instrument in place. That is the gap this work fills and the reason the form is a two-clock grid rather than a completeness figure.

verification.browser: Chromium, headless, scripting on and off
covers: the island: the JSON inside the page is byte-identical to data.json; no external script, stylesheet, media element or CSS fetch appears anywhere, and the only linked address in the whole document is the directive at EUR-Lex

the arithmetic, re-derived from the per-station records rather than read off the totals: spans, present and missing hours, the number of holes, the number that last exactly one hour, the run-length histogram accounting for every hour and every hole, the clock re-summed out of the wall, both capture denominators re-counted, and the exceedances re-added

the drawing: every cell of the served wall is decoded back out of the SVG to one distinct hour that really is missing somewhere, at exactly the shade its own station count demands, with no missing hour left undrawn

without a script: every headline number in the served text, the directive sentence quoted in full, the wall complete, both bar figures with the clock's bars checked against their own numbers, one tick per station on the capture strip with the right ones marked below the line, all 46 table rows, and the reading switch hidden because it cannot work

with a script: each of the three readings redraws the wall to exactly the hours its own series is true of, reports its own total, and places every cell at the right shade; pointing at three known cells reads back their date, hour and count
the network: no request off the filesystem in either state

the second door: all published daily maxima equal the largest hourly value of their day, none higher or lower, none without hours behind it, the day convention decided against plus and minus one day, and the eighteen-hour threshold shown to hold without exception above it
verification.determinism: build.py --check rebuilds data.json and index.html from counts.json and fails if one byte differs; the build reads nothing but counts.json and touches no network. measure.py rebuilds counts.json from the cache offline, and harvest.py --offline reloads the cache without the network.
